program_name: Animal Nutrition and Feed Safety is NOT a standalone degree. Its official name on the University of Turin application portal is 'Scienze animali (curriculum in Animal Nutrition and Feed Safety)' (apply.unito.it course id 670). The parent degree is the Italian-named 'Corso di Laurea Magistrale in Scienze Animali', whose official English rendering on the programme's own English microsite and in the UNITO catalogue is 'Master's Degree in Animal Science' (unito.it degree id 35837). The degree has exactly TWO curricula/tracks, and the official course sheet lists them explicitly: (1) 'Filiere zootecniche e qualita dei prodotti' ('Livestock supply chains and product quality'), delivered in ITALIAN; (2) 'Animal nutrition and feed safety', delivered in ENGLISH. So unlike Smart Agriculture (a mixed-language track inside Scienze agrarie), Animal Nutrition and Feed Safety is the single, wholly English-language track of an otherwise Italian degree. Internal degree-programme code [1707M22] for a.y. 2025/26 ([1707M21] for 2024/25 and earlier). Run jointly by the Department of Agricultural, Forest and Food Sciences (DISAFA) and the Department of Veterinary Sciences (Dipartimento di Scienze Veterinarie), within the School of Agriculture and Veterinary Medicine (Scuola di Agraria e Medicina Veterinaria, SAMEV). The diploma awarded is the LM-86 Laurea Magistrale in Scienze Animali, not a separately named 'Animal Nutrition and Feed Safety' degree.
level: master (second-cycle degree / Laurea Magistrale; 'POSTGRADUATE DEGREE' on apply.unito.it). Nominal duration 2 years, 120 ECTS, four semesters, starting in September. Mode: full-time, but apply.unito.it notes 'For each year of enrollment, students may choose between full-time or part-time status. Tuition fees vary accordingly.' Teaching delivery mode is 'convenzionale' (conventional / in-person), not blended or distance. It is a single-university UNITO degree, NOT an interuniversity or joint degree. A separate optional double-degree mobility scheme exists with VetAgro Sup (Clermont-Ferrand, France) leading to 'Ingenieur Agronome (Master/Bac+5 en Agronomie et Sciences Animales) from VetAgro Sup and the Master Degree in Animal science (LM-86) from the University of Turin', with a dedicated integrated career plan for the 'Animal Nutrition and Feed Safety' track - but that is an exchange scheme open only to students ALREADY enrolled at UNITO, selected by a separate annual Call, and capped at 3 Animal Science students per institution per year. It is not the structure of the degree itself and is not an entry route.
teaching_language: Case 2 in the taxonomy - an English-taught PATHWAY/CURRICULUM inside an Italian-named degree - BUT, unlike Smart Agriculture or Viticultural and Enological Sciences, this pathway appears to be delivered 100% in English for its full two years, not partially. Evidence: (a) apply.unito.it course 670 states 'Study language: English' and the machine-readable JSON feed carries "language": "en" (a single-language code), in direct contrast with course 681 (Smart Agriculture) which carries "language": "en~it" and displays 'combined English/Italian'; (b) the official course sheet ('Scheda del corso', last updated 09/03/2026) lists the parent degree's overall language as 'Lingua: italiano/inglese' and then splits it by track: '1) Percorso "Filiere zootecniche e qualita dei prodotti", erogato in lingua italiana; 2) Percorso "Animal nutrition and feed safety", erogato in lingua inglese' - i.e. the Italian/English label describes the DEGREE as a whole because it contains one Italian track and one English track, not because the English track itself is bilingual; (c) the English-language microsite en.san.unito.it renders the same as 'Language: Italian / English ... Curriculum: "Filiere zootecniche e qualita dei prodotti" Course, delivered in Italian; "Animal nutrition and feed safety" Course, delivered in English'; (d) the whole degree runs a dedicated English microsite (en.san.unito.it) with English admission, courses, exams and graduation pages, which is consistent with a genuinely English-taught track. Practical reading for an applicant: you can reasonably expect to complete the 120 ECTS in English on this track, and NO Italian language certificate or Italian exam is demanded at admission (apply.unito.it lists English ONLY under 'Language requirements', whereas Smart Agriculture lists 'English / Italian'). Italian remains useful for daily life, administration and internships/stages in Piedmont livestock and feed businesses, but it is not an admission requirement. [uncertain - the semester-by-semester 2026/27 study plan (piano di studi / manifesto degli studi) could not be fetched to prove that every single one of the 120 ECTS, including elective and thesis activities, is offered in English; www.san.unito.it/do/didattica.pl and the Insegnamenti page were unreachable both directly (network-level refusal) and via the Internet Archive (HTTP 429 rate limiting) at the time of research. The 'erogato in lingua inglese' wording and the single-code "en" language flag are strong but indirect evidence. Applicants should confirm with didattica.disafa@unito.it that free-choice credits and the thesis can be completed in English.]
campus: Grugliasco (Turin metropolitan area, Piedmont, Italy) - the Grugliasco agro-veterinary campus of the University of Turin, shared by DISAFA, the Department of Veterinary Sciences and the SAMEV school. The Italian course sheet states 'Sede didattica: Grugliasco'; the English microsite renders it 'Teaching venue: Grugliasco (Turin)'. apply.unito.it lists Institution location 'Italy, Turin' but Study location and Department location 'Italy, Grugliasco'. The University's legal/administrative seat is Via Verdi 8, 10124 Torino.
degree_class: LM-86 - Scienze zootecniche e tecnologie animali (English: 'Zootechnical sciences and animal technologies' / Animal Husbandry Sciences and Technologies), Italian second-cycle degree class, ordinamento D.M. 270. Confirmed on the official course sheet ('Classe: LM 86 - Scienze zootecniche e tecnologie animali'), on the English microsite ('Class: LM 86 - Zootechnical sciences and animal technologies') and on the double-degree page ('the Master Degree in Animal science (LM-86) from the University of Turin'). UNITO internal degree-programme code: [1707M22] for a.y. 2025/26 (previously [1707M21]). unito.it degree id: 35837. apply.unito.it course id: 670.
admission_type: Open access / free access ('accesso non programmato', also written 'accesso libero') SUBJECT TO verification of curricular requirements and of adequate personal preparation. Exact wording on the official pages: Italian - 'Il Corso di Laurea Magistrale in Scienze Animali e ad accesso non programmato' and 'Tipo di accesso: accesso libero, previa verifica dei requisiti curriculari ed adeguata preparazione'; English microsite - 'The Master's Degree Course in Animal Science is open to access' and 'Type of access: free access, subject to verification of curricular requirements and adequate preparation'. There is NO national numerus clausus, NO TOLC, NO SAT, NO GRE/GMAT and no ranked competitive selection call. However, open access does NOT mean automatic admission: admission is conditional on (a) meeting the minimum curricular requirements (requisiti curriculari minimi) documented by transcript, and (b) passing a mandatory oral admission interview assessing 'adequate personal preparation'. Enrolment with formative gaps ('carenze formative') is explicitly NOT permitted. In addition, for applicants going through the international Apply@UniTo route there is a HARD AUTOMATIC GRADE CUT-OFF that functions as a de-facto selection filter: 'Candidates whose ratio between the obtained CGPA and the maximum obtainable CGPA is lower than 0.8 will be automatically excluded from the selection.' For non-EU applicants residing abroad a separate quota applies (50 places, shared across both curricula - see academic_requirements). International applicants apply through the Apply@UniTo (DreamApply) portal within one of the University's fixed admission calls, plus - for visa applicants - Universitaly pre-enrolment; holders of Italian qualifications instead enrol directly via MyUniTo (myUniTo > Iscrizioni > Test valutazione).

entry_exam_or_test: No national or standardised entrance exam (no TOLC, no SAT, no GRE, no GMAT) and - unlike the sibling Scienze agrarie / Smart Agriculture programme - NO written multiple-choice test either. The assessment for Animal Science is a single ORAL ADMISSION INTERVIEW. Official wording (Requisiti di ammissione, page last updated 09/03/2026): 'La verifica dell'adeguatezza della preparazione personale sara svolta, attraverso un colloquio orale, da apposita Commissione nominata dal CCLM' - the adequacy of personal preparation is assessed through an oral interview by a Commission appointed by the degree programme council. apply.unito.it adds that the interview can be held remotely, which matters for overseas applicants: 'The evaluation Committee will also assess candidate's personal preparation through in-person and web interviews.' ATTEMPTS: 'Qualora il/la candidato/a non superi il colloquio di ammissione potra ripresentarsi nelle successive date calendarizzate: non sara consentito sostenere la prova di ammissione piu di n. 2 volte per ciascun anno accademico' - a failed candidate may re-sit on later scheduled dates, but no more than 2 attempts per academic year. INTERVIEW SYLLABUS (three areas, identical on the Italian and English pages): (1) Animal production / Produzioni animali - knowledge of farmed animals from the anatomical-physiological, morphological and functional point of view; nutritional profile of feed ingredients and nutritional requirements of the main farmed species; feed formulation/rationing; genetic improvement applied to qualitative and quantitative traits. (2) Vegetable/crop production / Produzioni vegetali - basic knowledge of forage production and forage systems in the various agricultural areas. (3) English language - comprehension and translation ability, including the disciplinary/technical lexicon. PRE-FILTER BEFORE THE INTERVIEW: for Apply@UniTo applicants, the CGPA ratio rule bites first - 'Candidates whose ratio between the obtained CGPA and the maximum obtainable CGPA is lower than 0.8 will be automatically excluded from the selection.' REMEDY FOR MISSING CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS: 'Qualora il/la candidato/a non sia in possesso degli specifici requisiti curriculari, su indicazione della Commissione per le carriere degli studenti (CCS) del Corso di Studio potra eventualmente frequentare singoli insegnamenti offerti dall'Ateneo e, una volta superato il relativo accertamento, potra accedere alla verifica della preparazione personale' - candidates lacking the curricular requirements may take single courses (singoli insegnamenti) offered by the University and, once passed, proceed to the personal-preparation check. [uncertain - the calendar of interview dates is published separately on the course website (Avvisi / Guida al corso di studio), which could not be fetched; and the 0.8 CGPA auto-exclusion appears ONLY in the apply.unito.it entry-qualification text, not in the Italian Requisiti di ammissione page, so it is unclear whether it applies to all applicants or only to those routed through Apply@UniTo. Detailed procedures are stated to be defined in the Study Program Regulations (Regolamento didattico), which was not located as a PDF.]
academic_requirements:
ENTRY QUALIFICATION. A three-year first-cycle degree (Laurea) or a three-year Diploma Universitario, or an equivalent foreign qualification recognised as suitable under current Italian law. apply.unito.it is more specific about the field than the Italian page: 'You must hold a first-cycle degree (i.e. bachelor's degree) in Animal Science or Agricultural Science or otherwise similar degrees gained after at least 3 years of University education. You will also need to meet specific admission requirements and demonstrate a suitable academic preparation and a solid background in agriculture and livestock production systems and skills in plant and animal productions as well as agriculture economy.' Enrolment with formative gaps ('carenze formative') is NOT permitted - requirements must be met in full before enrolment.

MINIMUM CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS (requisiti curriculari minimi) - a 60 ECTS rule split 20 + 40. The candidate must previously have obtained at least 60 CFU/ECTS in basic and/or characterising activities, distributed as follows.
(i) AT LEAST 20 ECTS in the Italian scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD) FIS/01, FIS/08, INF/01, MAT/01, MAT/09, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/02, VET/01, BIO/01, BIO/02, BIO/03, BIO/04, BIO/05, BIO/07, CHIM/03, CHIM/06, BIO/10, BIO/11, BIO/12, BIO/13. apply.unito.it renders these in English as: 'Experimental physics, Didactics and history of physics, Informatics, Mathematical logic, Operational research, Economics, Economic policy, Veterinary anatomy, General botany, Systematic botany, Environmental and applied botany, Plant physiology, Zoology, Ecology, General and inorganic chemistry, Organic chemistry, Biochemistry, Molecular biology, Clinical biochemistry and molecular biology, Experimental biology.'
(ii) AND AT LEAST 40 ECTS in the SSD VET/02, VET/03, VET/04, VET/05, VET/06, VET/07, AGR/01, AGR/02, AGR/07, AGR/09, AGR/10, AGR/11, AGR/13, AGR/15, AGR/16, AGR/17, AGR/18, AGR/19, AGR/20, ICAR/06. In English on apply.unito.it: 'Veterinary physiology, Veterinary pathology, Inspection of foods of animal origin, Infectious diseases of domestic animals, Parasitology and animal parasitic diseases, Veterinary pharmacology and toxicology, Agricultural economics and rural appraisal, Agronomy and field crops, Agricultural genetics, Agricultural machinery and mechanization, Rural buildings and agro-forest land planning, General and applied entomology, Agricultural chemistry, Food science and technology, Agricultural Microbiology, Livestock systems, animal breeding and genetics, Animal nutrition and feeding, Animal science, and Aquaculture, poultry and rabbit science.'
Note the emphasis: the 40-ECTS block is the heavier and more restrictive one, and it is dominated by veterinary (VET/*) and agricultural (AGR/*) sectors, especially animal science, animal nutrition, livestock systems and forage/crop production. A purely biological, food-technology or environmental bachelor's will usually satisfy the 20-ECTS block but fail the 40-ECTS block.

AUTOMATIC SATISFACTION BY ITALIAN DEGREE CLASS. 'I requisiti curriculari richiesti risultano soddisfatti per le classi di laurea L25, L38 e LM42 (nonche classi 20, 40 e 47/S dei precedenti ordinamenti)' - the curricular requirements are deemed automatically satisfied for Italian bachelor's classes L-25 (Agricultural and forestry sciences and technologies), L-38 (Zootechnical sciences and animal production technologies) and LM-42 (Veterinary Medicine), as well as the corresponding pre-reform classes 20, 40 and 47/S. For any OTHER class - which includes every foreign degree - 'il (CCLM) di Scienze Animali potra stabilire, sulla base dei programmi, l'equipollenza fra settori presenti negli ordinamenti di Lauree di classi diverse dalla L25, L38, LM42 ai fini dell'ammissione alle prove di accertamento della preparazione personale': the degree programme council decides equivalence CASE BY CASE on the basis of the course syllabi. This is the key discretionary step for international applicants and the reason course syllabi must be uploaded.

GRADE THRESHOLD - A HARD CUT-OFF EXISTS. Unusually for a UNITO open-access master's, apply.unito.it publishes an automatic numeric exclusion: 'Candidates whose ratio between the obtained CGPA and the maximum obtainable CGPA is lower than 0.8 will be automatically excluded from the selection.' In practice this means roughly 80% of the maximum grade in the applicant's own national scale - e.g. about 88/110 on the Italian scale, 3.2/4.0 US GPA, 80/100, or 8/10. This is stricter than most comparable UNITO programmes and should be treated as a genuine first-stage filter.

DIGITAL AND ENGLISH SKILLS PRESUMED. 'Sono date per acquisite un'adeguata capacita di utilizzo dei principali strumenti informatici (elaborazione di testi, utilizzo di fogli elettronici di calcolo, progettazione e gestione di database, utilizzo di strumenti di presentazione) ed una capacita di utilizzo fluente, in forma scritta e orale, della lingua inglese, corrispondente almeno al livello B2' - adequate command of the main IT tools (word processing, spreadsheets, database design and management, presentation tools) and fluent written and oral English at least at CEFR B2 are taken as acquired on entry.

PLACES AND NON-EU QUOTA. The degree is open access, so there is no overall cap on Italian/EU places. For non-EU applicants residing abroad there IS a quota: apply.unito.it 'Territory requirements' states 'This degree program has 50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad. These places are shared among all the curricula of this degree program.' Read this carefully: the 50 places belong to the whole Scienze animali / Animal Science LM-86 degree and are SHARED between the Italian-taught 'Filiere zootecniche e qualita dei prodotti' track and the English-taught 'Animal Nutrition and Feed Safety' track. There is no separate quota reserved for Animal Nutrition and Feed Safety alone, and no published figure for how many of the 50 have historically gone to this track.

DOCUMENT LANGUAGES. 'The entry qualification documents are accepted in the following languages: English / French / Italian / Spanish. If the document is issued in a different language from those listed above, you will have to upload both the original document and its certified translation.'

[uncertain - the 20/40 CFU SSD breakdown, the L-25/L-38/LM-42 automatic-satisfaction rule and the two-attempt cap come from the Italian 'Requisiti di ammissione' page whose own last-update stamp is 09/03/2026 (recent and therefore likely current for 2026/27), read via the Internet Archive because www.san.unito.it refuses direct fetches; the 2026/27 Didactic Regulation could restate them. Also uncertain: exactly how a foreign transcript is mapped onto Italian SSD codes - this is an explicitly case-by-case CCLM decision and no published conversion table exists. Finally, the 0.8 CGPA auto-exclusion is published only on apply.unito.it and does not appear on the Italian departmental page, so its scope (all applicants vs. Apply@UniTo applicants only) is not fully clear.]
language_requirements:
ENGLISH ONLY - no Italian requirement at admission. This is the clearest practical difference between this programme and the other partial-English UNITO agricultural pathways.

ENGLISH - WHAT IS ASKED. apply.unito.it 'Language requirements' lists a single language: 'English - Your knowledge of the English language will be verified during the admission interview.' The entry-qualification block adds: 'Adequate written and oral proficiency in English, including technical vocabulary, is also required.' The Italian regulation frames B2 as a presumed prerequisite: 'una capacita di utilizzo fluente, in forma scritta e orale, della lingua inglese, corrispondente almeno al livello B2' - fluent written and oral command of English corresponding to at least CEFR B2 is taken as acquired on entry. The interview syllabus explicitly includes 'Lingua inglese: capacita di traduzione e comprensione' (English: translation and comprehension ability).

HOW THE ENGLISH REQUIREMENT CAN BE SATISFIED - TWO ALTERNATIVE ROUTES. The English microsite gives an unusually concrete rule: 'An adequate knowledge of the English language is also required in both the written and the oral form with reference to the disciplinary lexicon. This requirement, whose verification methods are detailed in the Study Program Regulations, is considered satisfied if the students have taken AT LEAST ONE ENGLISH LANGUAGE EXAM IN THEIR UNIVERSITY CURRICULUM OR hold a certificate of knowledge of the English language at a level equal to B2 (at least) of the Common European Framework, issued by an accredited body.' So a documented university English exam on the bachelor's transcript is an accepted alternative to an IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge certificate. No minimum numeric score (e.g. IELTS 6.0, TOEFL 80) is published anywhere for this course. In practice, whatever the paperwork, the departmental admission interview is the operative check, and it is conducted with reference to the technical/disciplinary vocabulary of animal science.

ITALIAN - NOT REQUIRED. apply.unito.it lists English alone under Language requirements for course 670 (contrast course 681 / Smart Agriculture, which lists 'English / Italian'). No Italian language test, interview or certificate is imposed for admission to this curriculum. Furthermore, the CLIQ Italian B2 certificate obligation demonstrably does NOT apply here: UNITO scopes it as 'Non-EU applicants residing abroad (visa applicants) only. For undergraduate or 5-6-year postgraduate degree programs with free admission taught in Italian, an Italian language certificate at least at a B2 level, issued from 2023 onwards under the CLIQ quality system, is required.' Animal Nutrition and Feed Safety is a 2-year laurea magistrale taught in English, so it fails both conditions of that rule. Italian therefore remains a practical/daily-life and internship asset rather than an admission barrier.

[uncertain - the 'one university English exam OR a B2 certificate' rule comes from the en.san.unito.it Admission requirements page, whose own last-update stamp is 07/12/2021, so it is the oldest source used in this record even though it is fully consistent with the Italian page updated 09/03/2026 and with apply.unito.it. The page itself defers the detail to the 'Study Program Regulations' (Regolamento didattico), which could not be located as a PDF. Since no numeric certificate threshold is published, applicants without a transcript English exam should e-mail didattica.disafa@unito.it to confirm which certificate and score will be accepted before applying.]
required_documents:
Submitted through Apply@UniTo (apply.unito.it, DreamApply platform) for international applicants; holders of Italian qualifications instead attach documents to the MyUniTo online application (myUniTo > Iscrizioni > Test valutazione).

COURSE-SPECIFIC ITEMS FOR COURSE 670:
(1) The first-cycle/bachelor's degree certificate plus a full transcript of exams taken, detailed enough to demonstrate the 20 + 40 = 60 ECTS curricular requirement and to allow the Commission to map foreign courses onto Italian SSD codes.
(2) Copies of the syllabi / course programmes of the exams taken - the Italian page requires this explicitly for candidates coming from another university or department ('copia dei programmi dei corsi sostenuti'), and for foreign applicants it is effectively mandatory because the CCLM decides SSD equivalence 'sulla base dei programmi'.
(3) A MOTIVATION LETTER. This appears twice: apply.unito.it's course-level 'Other requirements' block states plainly 'A motivation letter must be added to your application', and the University-wide rules also require a motivation letter for all postgraduate programmes.
(4) Evidence of English proficiency - either a transcript showing at least one university English language exam, or a CEFR B2+ certificate from an accredited body.
(5) For the Italian route only: 'autocertificazione del titolo di studio e degli esami sostenuti' (self-certification of the qualification and of the exams taken).

GENERAL APPLY@UNITO REQUIREMENTS FOR ALL POSTGRADUATE APPLICANTS (news item 13, dated 29 January 2026):
(a) the documentation required for your specific foreign education system (secondary and university qualifications);
(b) 'motivation letter in English/Italian';
(c) 'additional documents required by some specific postgraduate degree programmes (please refer to "Entry qualification", "Language requirements" and "Other requirements" in the degree program description), such as: minimum credit requirements and English language certifications';
(d) 'further optional documentation: degree programme syllabus (course description) issued by the foreign Institution/University, provided with a translation into Italian, English, French or Spanish' - optional in general, but strongly advised here given the SSD equivalence assessment;
(e) payment of the non-refundable €60 application fee within the deadline of the call (the same €60 applies whether you select one or two degree programmes).

LANGUAGE OF DOCUMENTS. 'All documents uploaded in your online application are accepted in Italian, English, French or Spanish. If your documents are issued in a different language, an official translation in one of the above-mentioned languages is also required.' Entry-qualification documents specifically: English / French / Italian / Spanish, otherwise original plus certified translation.

AFTER SUBMISSION. 'Once you have submitted the application, please be aware that we might require you to upload further documents (declaration of value, statement of verification, statement of comparability issued by CIMEA, etc.)', and 'during the enrolment step, the International Students Office might request further documentation in addition to what was presented by applicants during the application step.'

VISA APPLICANTS (non-EU residing abroad) additionally complete Universitaly pre-enrolment and the visa file at the competent Italian diplomatic mission. No CLIQ Italian certificate is needed for this English-taught master's.

[uncertain - beyond the motivation letter, transcript and syllabi, no Animal-Nutrition-and-Feed-Safety-specific checklist (e.g. whether a CV or reference letters are expected) was found on any official page; the departmental 'Guida al corso di studio' and 'Modulistica' pages, which may carry an additional local checklist, could not be fetched because www.san.unito.it refuses direct requests and the Internet Archive began returning HTTP 429 during the session.]

uncertainty_notes:
1) PATHWAY, NOT A SEPARATE DEGREE - CONFIRMED. The research brief's hypothesis is correct. 'Animal Nutrition and Feed Safety' has no independent degree code, no independent admission call, no independent non-EU quota and no independent diploma. It is one of the two curricula inside the Italian-named master's degree 'Scienze Animali' / 'Animal Science' [1707M22], class LM-86. The diploma awarded is the LM-86 Laurea Magistrale in Scienze Animali. Aggregator sites market it as 'Master in Animal Nutrition and Feed Safety', which overstates its independence.

2) BUT THE LANGUAGE SITUATION IS BETTER THAN FOR SMART AGRICULTURE AND VITICULTURAL AND ENOLOGICAL SCIENCES - THIS IS THE KEY DIFFERENCE. Whereas Smart Agriculture is explicitly a mixed track (apply.unito.it: 'combined English/Italian', JSON "language": "en~it", only about 60 of 120 ECTS in English, first semester in Italian), Animal Nutrition and Feed Safety is presented as the WHOLLY ENGLISH track: apply.unito.it says 'Study language: English' with the single-language JSON code "en", and the official course sheet says the track is 'erogato in lingua inglese'. The parent degree's 'italiano/inglese' label describes the coexistence of one Italian track and one English track, not a bilingual delivery of this track. This should be presented to users as a genuinely English-taught option, with the caveat in point 3.

3) WHAT COULD NOT BE PROVEN ABOUT THE LANGUAGE. The semester-by-semester 2026/27 study plan was NOT retrievable, so there is no direct proof that all 120 ECTS - including elective/free-choice credits, internships/stages and the thesis - are available in English. The 'delivered in English' wording plus the "en" language flag are strong indirect evidence, but a student should confirm with didattica.disafa@unito.it before committing, particularly about free-choice credits and thesis supervision. Note also that internships and stages in Piedmont livestock and feed companies will in practice often require working Italian, even if the taught courses do not.

4) NO ITALIAN REQUIREMENT AT ADMISSION - A REAL ADVANTAGE. apply.unito.it lists English ONLY under 'Language requirements' for course 670, unlike course 681 (Smart Agriculture) which lists 'English / Italian' and warns both will be tested at interview. The CLIQ Italian B2 certificate rule does not apply either, because it covers only Italian-taught undergraduate and 5-6-year single-cycle programmes. For a non-Italian-speaking applicant, this programme is therefore substantially more accessible than the other UNITO agricultural English pathways.

5) THE 0.8 CGPA CUT-OFF IS THE STRICTEST PUBLISHED FILTER AND DESERVES PROMINENCE. 'Candidates whose ratio between the obtained CGPA and the maximum obtainable CGPA is lower than 0.8 will be automatically excluded from the selection.' Roughly 80% of the maximum grade in the applicant's own scale (about 88/110 Italian, 3.2/4.0 US, 80/100, 8/10). This is unusual for a nominally open-access UNITO master's and functions as a hard first-stage rejection. It appears only on apply.unito.it and NOT on the Italian departmental Requisiti di ammissione page, so its exact scope (all applicants, or only those applying through Apply@UniTo) is not fully clear and is flagged as uncertain.

6) 'OPEN ACCESS' IS MISLEADING WITHOUT CONTEXT. The degree is legally 'accesso non programmato' (no numerus clausus, no TOLC, no ranked competition), but admission still requires (a) clearing the 0.8 CGPA filter, (b) documenting the 20 + 40 = 60 ECTS curricular requirement, and (c) passing a compulsory oral interview, with a maximum of two attempts per academic year. Unlike Scienze agrarie, there is NO written 50-question test here - the assessment is oral only.

7) CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS ARE NARROW AND VETERINARY/ZOOTECHNICAL-HEAVY. The 40-ECTS block is dominated by VET/* and AGR/* sectors (animal nutrition and feeding, animal science, livestock systems, veterinary physiology/pathology, forage crops). Only Italian classes L-25, L-38 and LM-42 (plus old 20, 40, 47/S) satisfy the requirement automatically; every foreign degree is assessed case by case by the CCLM on the basis of course syllabi, with no published conversion table. Applicants from adjacent fields (general biology, food science, environmental science, agricultural engineering) should request a pre-assessment before applying and must upload detailed syllabi.

8) NON-EU APPLICANTS HAVE ONLY ONE WINDOW AND IT HAS ALREADY CLOSED FOR 2026/27. The single 2026/27 window open to non-EU citizens residing abroad closed on 29 January 2026 (opened 25 November 2025). The August-September 2026 window is explicitly reserved to Italians, EU/EU-equivalents and non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy. Since today is 1 September 2026, a non-EU applicant abroad must target the 2027/28 first call (expected late November 2026 - late January 2027 by analogy, not yet published). Conversely, EU/EU-equivalent applicants CAN still apply for 2026/27 until 8 September 2026, 23:59:59 CET - a live, time-critical window at the moment of writing.

9) THE 50 NON-EU PLACES ARE SHARED BETWEEN BOTH TRACKS. apply.unito.it is explicit that the 50 places for non-European applicants residing abroad belong to the whole Animal Science degree and are shared across all its curricula, i.e. between the Italian 'Filiere zootecniche e qualita dei prodotti' track and the English 'Animal Nutrition and Feed Safety' track. There is no track-specific allocation and no published historical split.

10) TWO DEPARTMENTS, ONE CAMPUS. Unusually, the degree is referenced to BOTH the Department of Veterinary Sciences and DISAFA (apply.unito.it names only DISAFA), under the SAMEV school, all on the Grugliasco campus. This matters for contacts: teaching office didattica.disafa@unito.it, +39 011 670 8911 / 9267.

11) ACCESS TOOLS AND SOURCE FRESHNESS. Everything from apply.unito.it (the HTML course page, the JSON feed for course 670, and news items 26, 13 and 53) was fetched LIVE and is the most reliable layer of this record; the course record's own update stamp is 23 June 2026. The san.unito.it and en.san.unito.it microsite pages refuse direct automated requests and were read through the Internet Archive; their own last-update stamps are 09/03/2026 for both Italian pages used (recent, and therefore likely valid for 2026/27), 16/05/2025 for the International students page, and 07/12/2021 for the English Admission requirements page (the oldest source used, though its content is consistent with the March 2026 Italian page). www.unito.it, en.unito.it and unito.coursecatalogue.cineca.it stay 403/405, so the UNITO catalogue entry (degree id 35837) and the tuition pages were confirmed only through search snippets. The Internet Archive began returning failures/HTTP 429 during the session, which is why the study plan (didattica.pl / Insegnamenti) and the 'Guida al corso di studio' could not be retrieved. The programme's Didactic Regulation (Regolamento didattico / Study Program Regulations) PDF, referenced by the English page as the authority on English-proficiency verification methods, was not located.

12) FEES FOR 2026/27 NOT YET PUBLISHED, AND THE RULES ARE CHANGING. Only the 2025/26 range (€156-€2,800 per year, income-dependent) is confirmed. Search snippets of en.unito.it indicate that from 2026-2027 the ISEE Parificato will no longer be used to reduce tuition fees and that applicants resident abroad will have the contribution applied directly on the basis of their country's GDP per capita PPP; students from 'particularly poor countries' may pay only the €156 first instalment. This is a material change for international applicants but was read from snippets only and must be re-verified on en.unito.it.

13) CONTACT POINTS FOR VERIFICATION. Animal Science coordinator Prof.ssa Joana Maria Venda Da Graca Nery (joana.nery@unito.it, +39 011 670 9261); departmental teaching office didattica.disafa@unito.it (+39 011 670 8911 / 9267); International Students Office internationalstudents@unito.it; incoming-student buddy service buddy.agrovet@unito.it. apply.unito.it also offers a chatbot for course-specific questions.
